# OA v0.7.22

**Status:** Source snapshot; hosted publication blocked

**Release date:** 2026-08-28

**Source:** [`v0.7.22`](https://github.com/realminc/oa/tree/v0.7.22)

## Summary

OA v0.7.22 is the immutable hosted-release repair for the blocked v0.7.21
foundation candidate. It publishes the same foundation hardening, host-memory,
VKL/VMA boundary, allocator-cache, and `oa::Vector` migration while restoring
the dependency ratchet required by the hosted build.

Product APIs, VMA allocation algorithms, numerical behavior, and recorded
performance results are unchanged from the v0.7.21 source snapshot.

The hosted Release, package, UBSAN, CPU-Vulkan, and Python-wheel jobs passed.
The ASAN job completed 271 of 272 `TestOaStd` cases without a sanitizer finding,
then CTest terminated the executable at its 120-second per-test limit. Release
publication was therefore skipped. The immutable repair is v0.7.23.

## Fixed

- VMA placement construction uses OA's language-level placement tag rather than
  the hosted `<new>` header.
- The VMA provenance manifest records the corrected exact hashes for
  `detail/config.h` and `detail/containers.h`.
- The hosted OA standard-library audit again observes zero `<new>` includes in
  the derived VMA configuration instead of rejecting the candidate before its
  build stage.

## Compatibility and migration

- Replace `oa::Vec<T>` with `oa::Vector<T>`.
- Replace `<oa/core/std/vec.h>` with `<oa/core/std/vector.h>`.
- No compatibility alias or forwarding header is provided. Rebuild native
  consumers and discard pre-1.0 binary caches.
- Public OA allocator ownership and Vulkan value contracts are unchanged; VMA
  and VKL remain private implementation dependencies.

## Performance

No performance claim changes in this repair. The complete fixed-host results,
process ranges, correctness oracles, rejected experiments, and limitations are
published in the [foundation benchmark](../benchmarks/oaStd.md) and summarized
in the [v0.7.21 source note](v0.7.21.md).

## Verification

| Gate | Result | Evidence scope |
|---|---|---|
| Dependency ratchet | Pass | vendored hosted includes reduced from 125 to 124; VMA `<new>` baseline restored to zero |
| VMA façade | Pass | 5/5 Release tests |
| VMA internals | Pass | 2/2 Release tests |
| Runtime allocator | Pass | 21/21 Release tests on Intel Iris Xe with live Vulkan allocation and transfer paths |
| Public snapshot | Required before publication | private-path, secret, symlink, version, docs, generator, and header gates |
| Hosted release | Workflow-owned | complete build, sanitizers, CPU-Vulkan, packages, wheel, PyPI, assets, and checksums |

## Known limitations

- Linux x86-64 remains the qualified runtime host for the new foundation and
  VMA measurements. Other OS, compiler, architecture, driver, and device
  matrices remain open.
- Binary independence, extended allocation-fault injection, long-running fuzz
  campaigns, and hostile-input qualification remain unfinished.
- The retained fixed-host performance gaps and security/performance tradeoffs
  are unchanged from v0.7.21.
- Vulkan Video and GPU paths remain capability-, queue-, driver-, and
  device-dependent; unsupported routes fail closed.

## Upgrade

Rebuild C++ and Python consumers, apply the `oa::Vector` source migration,
regenerate owned sources, and discard stale build, package, execution-plan,
model, checkpoint, and pre-1.0 binary caches.
